correctness.rationale: For odd B, multiplicativity forces each beta(p^e) to be a power of two. Even e gives an odd integer greater than one. For odd e=2t+1 the geometric factor in beta(p^e) has 2-adic valuation v2(t+1), by repeatedly halving its geometric length and using p^2=1 mod 8. If t>0 the factor exceeds t+1, so it is not a power of two. Thus B is a squarefree product of Fermat primes, with the indices forced by the set bits of a-1. For even a>=4, beta(2^a) is 11 mod 16 while the prescribed product is 3 or 15. For odd a>1, at the first omitted index j below the top digit, beta(2^a) is -1/3 modulo 2^(2^j+1); the forced product is the prefix without F_j, which differs from -1/3 by an odd multiple of 2^(2^j). This forces a=2^k-1. The product then is F_1 through F_(k-1); pairwise coprimality and composite F_5 exclude every k>=6, irrespective of later Fermat primes. Independently checked primality by trial division of each F_0 through F_4 up to its square root, the exact factorization F_5=641*6700417, and the two iterates for all asserted exponents, including 31. The frozen finite script, inspected but not executed, is corroboration rather than the exclusion proof.
